_comment: dialog_sized keeps ordinary app windows from matching; every rule also has to survive CONFIRM_SCANS polls (see yolo_watch.py). UserNotificationCenter was the main source of false 'approval needed' alerts, so it is dialog-gated too.
_auto_approve: auto_approve clicks the dialog's Allow/OK button and pushes an after-the-fact alert naming what was granted. It only ever clicks a button whose exact title is in ALLOW_BUTTONS, needs Accessibility permission, and is switched off by `touch ~/.yolo_mode_no_autoapprove` or the menubar toggle.
_catch_all: The last rule is a catch-all: any dialog-shaped window showing an Allow/OK button gets approved, whoever owns it. owner_not carves out the three kinds that stay manual. SecurityAgent, loginwindow and Keychain are how macOS asks Nathan to prove he is Nathan -- a watcher that clicks those turns his password prompt into a formality for whatever asked. 1Password releases vault secrets, so it stays manual EXCEPT the explicit 'Access Requested / Allow ... to get CLI access' dialog, which is auto-Authorized by its own rule above (buttons=['Authorize'] only, so Unlock and other 1Password prompts are untouched). CoreServicesUIAgent is Gatekeeper, where the Allow-shaped button runs a program that was just downloaded, which is how a drive-by download becomes a running program. Everything else -- screen recording, mic, camera, files, automation, Shortcuts -- is auto-approved.
